It receives every image and can serve none. This is STRUCTURAL, not a lapsed chore: App installation tokens authenticate docker login but are DENIED docker pull on private repo-linked packages (ADR-088 arm-b), so no zero-touch GHCR pull credential can exist — only a personal one. Consequence: zot is the SOLE pull path and the CI zot mirror is now release-blocking (ADR-096 amendment 2026-07-30). OCI-native container registry (zot) on a dedicated Hetzner host (cx33, 4 vCPU / 8 GB, hel1, volume-backed) on the private network (10.0.1.30:5000), behind a deny-all-public firewall — the zero-touch machine-credential registry that replaces GHCR on the pull path (ADR-096, #6122). Sized cx33 in hel1 (#6288 — the plan's cx32 target does not exist as a Hetzner type; cx33 is the real 8 GB type, offered in hel1 not nbg1) with an ADR-062 --memory=7168m cap so zot's ~35 GB store boot scan cannot host-OOM restart-loop the box. The 60 GB store volume re-fills ONLY from a fresh CI dual-push — NOT from GHCR. Its previous description as a 'disposable GHCR mirror' with an 'atomic GHCR fallback' is RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (#7071): the sibling ghcr node in this same enumeration is now marked DEAD AS A FALLBACK (read PAT revoked -> 401, minter disabled -> 403 DENIED), so an emptied store leaves NO registry any host can pull from until CI re-pushes. The blobs stay reproducible, so this is a recoverability property, never a free one — every recut/replace of this volume takes production's only pull path offline for the gap. Hosts pull the SAME @sha256 digests here (crane-copy from CI preserves them); cosign verifies the zot-stored .sig offline against the unchanged pinned root. Plain-HTTP on the private net (integrity via cosign digest-pinning, not TLS). AT REST: guest-side LUKS, CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING (`hcloud_volume.registry` is declared RAW — no `format` — and cloud-init-registry.yml luksFormats/luksOpens it as /dev/mapper/registry, keyed by random_password.registry_luks via doppler_secret.registry_luks_key). The LIVE device is still plaintext ext4 until the guarded `registry-luks-recut` workflow_dispatch is fired; that vehicle shipped UNFIRED (#6929), so this is a code-declared posture, NOT a live-verified one. Low sensitivity (our own OCI blobs + cosign signatures, no user/repo data); integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not at-rest encryption (encryption-posture-ledger.json)

ACME CA issuing the GitHub Pages custom-domain TLS cert for soleur.ai/www (ADR-125, #6657/#6698). Validation is HTTP-01 against GitHub's origin, which is why remediation must transiently flip apex+www to DNS-only — a Cloudflare-proxied record makes LE see CF anycast instead of GitHub's 185.199.x. TWO properties drive the design: (1) LE PREFERS IPv6 and retries over IPv4 only on a NETWORK-level failure of the first request (redirects get no retry), so a proxied AAAA that answers 200 with the wrong content defeats validation at any window length with no fallback — the propagation gate therefore requires AAAA ENODATA and treats a surviving AAAA as terminal, not retryable; (2) failed-validation rate limits are 5 per identifier per account per hour, refilling ~1 per 12 min with a compounding daily cap, and GitHub surfaces NONE of it — `GET /pages` returns the same `bad_authz` string whether the cause is DNS, timing, or a rate-limit pause. That invisibility is why probe-only mode (which consumes no validation attempt) is the DEFAULT for manual fires.

Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 and Google 8.8.8.8, queried via node:dns Resolver.setServers() by cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue's DNS-propagation gate (#6698). Used to confirm the DNS-only flip actually reached the public internet before the cert poll begins — Cloudflare's TTL for proxied records is fixed at 300 s, so a proxy-status flip takes ~5-10 min to propagate and a poll started before then is guaranteed-wasted public-TLS-outage window. `dig` is deliberately NOT used: it is not installed in the app image (the Dockerfile installs only ca-certificates, git, bubblewrap, socat, qpdf, jq), so shelling out would throw at runtime.

External uptime/heartbeat monitoring (BetterStackHQ/better-uptime) AND a Logs warehouse (source 2457081, ClickHouse-SQL-queryable) that CI polls read-only. Apex + inngest + registry-disk heartbeats, plus (#6438/#6548) TWO new per-host web heartbeats — web_zot_consumer (the zot-consumer serviceability probe, #6438 §1) and web_nic_guard (the §3 private-NIC-guard liveness beat, #6438 §3), both for_each var.web_hosts — and git-data, whose git_data_prd beat is FED by the web-host consumer probe (#6548) but is **deliberately NOT armed** — #6982 (D-HB) withdrew the plan to arm it, and #6548 alone now owns the decision. Three reasons, any one disqualifying: the `arm_one` call for it lives in the PER-MERGE apply job, so creating the heartbeat would make an unborn flag-off host's health a merge-blocking dependency for the whole repository; a TCP connect-and-close to :22 proves the port is OPEN, not that git transport SERVES, and sshd is up before runcmd runs — so a host whose LUKS never mounted answers on :22 and beats GREEN, installing a green light over the exact failure the interlock exists to catch; and the object pool may be at 10/10. git-data's boot correctness is instead reported HOST-SIDE by its own emitter (#6982). Registry-liveness remains paused until #6537's feeder ships and a beat is measured. All three new/newly-fed web beats (web_zot_consumer, web_nic_guard, git_data_prd) are arm-gated by the automated measure-then-arm PATCH in apply-web-platform-infra.yml (ADR-117 amendment #6438). ALSO a per-host origin absence detector that probes each web host's CF-proxied hostname (web-N.app.soleur.ai/health) directly, so a dead/never-booted host pages with per-host attribution the round-robin monitors cannot give (#5933 Item 1). The Logs source receives SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK + SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC self-reports from the deny-all registry host AND SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC from web-1 (the §3 web-host guard, detect+emit+alarm, NO reboot — ADR-123) and is polled from GitHub Actions via betterstack-query.sh for the zot restart-loop recurrence alarm (#6291) + follow-through soak probes — log-content recurrence alarms are in-repo GH-cron pollers, not native Better Stack alerts (ADR-096).

Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.

description.txt: Zero-trust inbound access — no exposed ports. ONE tunnel (tunnel.tf) with THREE ingress rules (deploy./ssh./registry.). DETERMINISM IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not one-connector: since #6594/PR-A all three ingress services are ORIGIN-RELATIVE (deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000, ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22, registry. → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000), so whichever connector replica CF selects proxies to the correct origin (ADR-114 I2 discharged for all three). This — not 'localhost: means this host' — is what makes the management plane deterministic. NOT AN INVARIANT: the earlier 'exactly ONE connector, ADR-114 I1 enforced #6425' claim is FALSE in production. The server.tf web_tunnel_connector gate lives at cloud-init create-time user_data only, and hcloud_server.web carries ignore_changes=[user_data], so it never re-runs on a booted host. (Historical: web-2 booted 2026-07-13 BEFORE the gate merged 2026-07-15, so TWO connectors were live and measured; web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463) and var.web_hosts is now single-host.) I1 is a construction-time gate presented as a runtime precondition — it governs only future fresh hosts, and that stays true after #6441: the NIC gate added there is FIRST-BOOT (runcmd is once-per-instance), so a fresh connector host now waits for its private address before registering and DEFERS rather than aborting on timeout, but no gate re-runs on a host that is already up. CF binds ingress to a TUNNEL and picks a connector per edge colo; before the origin-relative pin a SECOND connector silently made every non-fan-out route (deploy-status, inngest-liveness, infra-config WRITEs, ssh.) answer from whichever replica the caller's colo selected — #6425 (16h of false inngest-down alarms), #6594 (a false-green infra-config apply), #6416. Origin-relative ingress makes that harmless: the coin flip no longer determines correctness. Standing guard: the */15 connector census in scheduled-inngest-health.yml (vantage-independent; a response-poll is colo-sticky and proves nothing). Management plane only: app.soleur.ai does NOT traverse the tunnel (direct CF-proxied A record, dns.tf); no cloudflared on zot/git-data/inngest (ADR-096).

description.txt: Cluster of Hetzner Cloud hosts (Nomad clients, spread placement) running web app + CLI engine containers. Per-user worktrees are host-local in the ADR-068 §1 sense (they do NOT live on the shared git-data host) but they are NOT on the root NVMe — they sit on a per-host ATTACHED BLOCK VOLUME, workspacesVolume below (#6588 corrected this description, which said 'host-local NVMe' and led readers to conclude there was no volume to encrypt). At first boot a fresh host pulls the web app image from GHCR and extracts its baked bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl via docker cp (ADR-080, #5921) — a path web-1 can never take: cx33 is unorderable in all 3 EU DCs and lifecycle{ignore_changes=[user_data]} means cloud-init never re-runs, so the bake reaches no live host (ADR-119 §(e)). ADR-143 (adopting, #6459) governs the return of a second web host: because cx33 is unorderable, web-2 returns as a fresh cattle **cpx22** (2c/4g x86, ~€19.49/mo net) — sized to web-1's MEASURED usage (~1.5 GB peak RAM / 0.48 load15 over 30d, not its over-provisioned 8g shape; ADR-143 D1) — a health-monitored standby at serving-weight 0 (NOT in the ingress rotation) until ADR-068 Phase-3 GA, since the sole-copy workspace volume lives on web-1 and a request routed to web-2 pre-flip would hit an empty workspace. TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-07-26 (ADR-143 addendum, #6966), FORCED BY STOCK: the live probe that day (/v1/datacenters .server_types.available) found the ENTIRE cx line — cx23 as well as cx33 — and the ENTIRE cax ARM line orderable in 0 of 3 EU DCs, so the earlier 'cx23, in stock in hel1' claim recorded here is FALSE and is retired. cpx22 matches cx23 on cores and RAM exactly (2c/4g) and doubles local disk, so the D1 sizing rationale is unchanged — this was a price change (+€14.00/mo), not a resize. Read .server_types.available, never .supported (the hcloud CLI has the same trap). A fresh cpx22 CAN take the docker-cp bake path (unlike the frozen web-1). NOTE the DR gap the same probe exposes: web-1 (cx33), soleur-grok-dogfood (cx33) and soleur-registry (cx23) all run on types that can no longer be ordered — they run fine but NONE can be rebuilt on its current type (#6460). The fleet remains single-host until web-2 is provisioned by the gated web-host-create dispatch

description.txt: Every user's checked-out repository. SOLE-COPY: refs/checkpoints/* is pushed by no refspec, session-sync.ts autocommits only knowledge-base/**, and signup-provisioned workspaces have no git remote at all — so ADR-068 §1's 'GitHub remains the durable rehydration source' does NOT hold here and there is no durable second copy anywhere (no upstream to rehydrate from). ENCRYPTED AT REST as of the 2026-07-23 cutover — the gap #6588/ADR-119 opened (PLAINTEXT ext4 while the published privacy policy claimed LUKS) is closed. HISTORY: an earlier 2026-07-20 cutover attempt (run 29782780158) landed /mnt/data on crypto_LUKS for ~27 minutes before its own dead-man timer silently remounted the retained plaintext volume over it (#6812) — do not cite that landing as the current state. The 2026-07-23 cutover is the one that certified: `workspaces-luks-verify` run **30040444418** reported `SOLEUR_WORKSPACES_READYZ ready=true writable=true populated=true workspace_count=8 expected=8` against `/dev/mapper/workspaces` — a mechanically measured verdict, not an assumed one (this distinction, per ADR-140, is the whole feature). web-2's instance was knowingly left plaintext (never served, empty) until its 2026-07-17 teardown (#6538/#6463). The fleet is single-host as of this writing, so no plaintext member remains — but that is a statement about the CURRENT fleet, NOT an invariant: the fresh web-2 (repinned cpx22, #6966) is born with its own per-host workspaces volume (hcloud_volume.workspaces, web-2 key) as RAW/empty PLAINTEXT, because the guest-side LUKS path for a FRESH host is the deferred #6931 work (ADR-141 D3) and the workspaces_luks attachment is web-1-bound and outside the birth fan-out (#6964). That member holds NO user data (sole copy is web-1's volume; web-2 is never routed pre-flip, dns.tf app record is web-1-only and the #6575 anti-pooling gate fail-closes), and it MUST NOT take serving weight while plaintext — re-evaluate at the ADR-068 Phase-3 GA flip

platform.infra.gitDataStore.technology: Bare git repos over private net

description.txt: Shared bare git repos (objects/refs) over the private net; per-user worktrees stay host-local on NVMe. The git-data host holds the per-ref monotonic max generation and writer-side-CAS-rejects stale lease writes (ADR-068). NOT YET PROVISIONED (#6977): this element is DECLARED in IaC and the host has never existed — an authenticated `terraform state list` returns zero git-data members — so every behaviour described here is the TARGET state, not the live one. It remains unborn until the gated `git-data-host-create` dispatch runs. The birth-readiness interlock that held that route is RELEASED by #6982, which ships the off-host emitter (ADR-149 item 1): the host now emits boot-stage fatals to Sentry from a baked DSN, a `stage:boot_complete` signal the birth job POLLS, and gc faults to Better Stack — so a green apply and a dark host are no longer indistinguishable. What holds the route now is MECHANICAL, not prose: `git_data_rung2_rehearsal_gate` (#6982 A3) runs in the same dispatch job before any provider is contacted and refuses unless `git-data-rung2-boot-evidence.env` attests a rung-2 boot rehearsal hash-bound to the CURRENT template — a hash-of-hashes over the cloud-init plus every `file()`-bound payload, so the evidence self-invalidates on any later edit to what ships. That file is absent, so a dispatch exits 1. #7025 shipped the gated rehearsal ROUTE that produces it (a separate Terraform root + `workflow_dispatch`), deliberately UNFIRED — a PR merges atomically, so evidence committed alongside its own harness would attest a rehearsal that never ran. The runbook banner is the THIRD hold, not the only one. AT REST: the target store is PLAINTEXT ext4 (`hcloud_volume.git_data`, `format = "ext4"`, no LUKS apparatus) — a fresh `hcloud_volume.git_data_luks` cutover target is declared alongside it (git-data-luks.tf) but is not the live store (`GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` gates the cutover). Ledgered exception (encryption-posture-ledger.json, tracking #6897), pending cutover

Its conditions are New/ExistingHighPriorityIssueCondition, i.e. FIRST-SEEN and ESCALATED-TO — NOT a recurrence of an issue that is already high priority. Since Sentry derives high priority from level, it is what actually routes a level=error event carrying no matching tag filter (the release-outcome mirror among them), and a repeat of an identical event is silent on this route. It is UI-managed, so ADR-031's IaC-is-the-source-of-truth posture does not cover it; tracked as #7142. NB IssueOwners has no ownership rule on this project, so the fallthrough is what actually reaches a human: a NoOne rule fires and pages nobody, by design there and a defect anywhere else. description.txt: Zero-trust inbound access — no exposed ports. ONE tunnel (tunnel.tf) with THREE ingress rules (deploy./ssh./registry.). DETERMINISM IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not one-connector: since #6594/PR-A all three ingress services are ORIGIN-RELATIVE (deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000, ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22, registry. → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000), so whichever connector replica CF selects proxies to the correct origin (ADR-114 I2 discharged for all three). This — not 'localhost: means this host' — is what makes the management plane deterministic. NOT AN INVARIANT: the earlier 'exactly ONE connector, ADR-114 I1 enforced #6425' claim is FALSE in production. The server.tf web_tunnel_connector gate lives at cloud-init create-time user_data only, and hcloud_server.web carries ignore_changes=[user_data], so it never re-runs on a booted host. (Historical: web-2 booted 2026-07-13 BEFORE the gate merged 2026-07-15, so TWO connectors were live and measured; web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463) and var.web_hosts is now single-host.) I1 is a construction-time gate presented as a runtime precondition — it governs only future fresh hosts, and that stays true after #6441: the NIC gate added there is FIRST-BOOT (runcmd is once-per-instance), so a fresh connector host now waits for its private address before registering and DEFERS rather than aborting on timeout, but no gate re-runs on a host that is already up. CF binds ingress to a TUNNEL and picks a connector per edge colo; before the origin-relative pin a SECOND connector silently made every non-fan-out route (deploy-status, inngest-liveness, infra-config WRITEs, ssh.) answer from whichever replica the caller's colo selected — #6425 (16h of false inngest-down alarms), #6594 (a false-green infra-config apply), #6416. Origin-relative ingress makes that harmless: the coin flip no longer determines correctness. Standing guard: the */15 connector census in scheduled-inngest-health.yml (vantage-independent; a response-poll is colo-sticky and proves nothing). Management plane only: app.soleur.ai does NOT traverse the tunnel (direct CF-proxied A record, dns.tf); no cloudflared on zot/git-data/inngest (ADR-096).

description.txt: Shared bare git repos (objects/refs) over the private net; per-user worktrees stay host-local on NVMe. The git-data host holds the per-ref monotonic max generation and writer-side-CAS-rejects stale lease writes (ADR-068). NOT YET PROVISIONED (#6977): this element is DECLARED in IaC and the host has never existed — an authenticated `terraform state list` returns zero git-data members — so every behaviour described here is the TARGET state, not the live one. It remains unborn until the gated `git-data-host-create` dispatch runs. The birth-readiness interlock that held that route is RELEASED by #6982, which ships the off-host emitter (ADR-149 item 1): the host now emits boot-stage fatals to Sentry from a baked DSN, a `stage:boot_complete` signal the birth job POLLS, and gc faults to Better Stack — so a green apply and a dark host are no longer indistinguishable. What holds the route now is MECHANICAL, not prose: `git_data_rung2_rehearsal_gate` (#6982 A3) runs in the same dispatch job before any provider is contacted and refuses unless `git-data-rung2-boot-evidence.env` attests a rung-2 boot rehearsal hash-bound to the CURRENT template — a hash-of-hashes over the cloud-init plus every `file()`-bound payload, so the evidence self-invalidates on any later edit to what ships. That file is absent, so a dispatch exits 1. #7025 shipped the gated rehearsal ROUTE that produces it (a separate Terraform root + `workflow_dispatch`), deliberately UNFIRED — a PR merges atomically, so evidence committed alongside its own harness would attest a rehearsal that never ran. The runbook banner is the THIRD hold, not the only one. AT REST: the target store is PLAINTEXT ext4 (`hcloud_volume.git_data`, `format = "ext4"`, no LUKS apparatus) — a fresh `hcloud_volume.git_data_luks` cutover target is declared alongside it (git-data-luks.tf) but is not the live store (`GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` gates the cutover). The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). OCI-native container registry (zot) on a dedicated Hetzner host (cx33, 4 vCPU / 8 GB, hel1, volume-backed) on the private network (10.0.1.30:5000), behind a deny-all-public firewall — the zero-touch machine-credential registry that replaces GHCR on the pull path (ADR-096, #6122). Sized cx33 in hel1 (#6288 — the plan's cx32 target does not exist as a Hetzner type; cx33 is the real 8 GB type, offered in hel1 not nbg1) with an ADR-062 --memory=7168m cap so zot's ~35 GB store boot scan cannot host-OOM restart-loop the box. The 60 GB store volume re-fills ONLY from a fresh CI dual-push — NOT from GHCR. Its previous description as a 'disposable GHCR mirror' with an 'atomic GHCR fallback' is RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (#7071): the sibling ghcr node in this same enumeration is now marked DEAD AS A FALLBACK (read PAT revoked -> 401, minter disabled -> 403 DENIED), so an emptied store leaves NO registry any host can pull from until CI re-pushes. The blobs stay reproducible, so this is a recoverability property, never a free one — every recut/replace of this volume takes production's only pull path offline for the gap. Hosts pull the SAME @sha256 digests here (crane-copy from CI preserves them); cosign verifies the zot-stored .sig offline against the unchanged pinned root. Plain-HTTP on the private net (integrity via cosign digest-pinning, not TLS). AT REST: guest-side LUKS, CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING (`hcloud_volume.registry` is declared RAW — no `format` — and cloud-init-registry.yml luksFormats/luksOpens it as /dev/mapper/registry, keyed by random_password.registry_luks via doppler_secret.registry_luks_key). The LIVE device is still plaintext ext4 until the guarded `registry-luks-recut` workflow_dispatch is fired; that vehicle shipped UNFIRED (#6929), so this is a code-declared posture, NOT a live-verified one. Three reasons, any one disqualifying: the `arm_one` call for it lives in the PER-MERGE apply job, so creating the heartbeat would make an unborn flag-off host's health a merge-blocking dependency for the whole repository; a TCP connect-and-close to :22 proves the port is OPEN, not that git transport SERVES, and sshd is up before runcmd runs — so a host whose LUKS never mounted answers on :22 and beats GREEN, installing a green light over the exact failure the interlock exists to catch; and the object pool may be at 10/10. git-data's boot correctness is instead reported HOST-SIDE by its own emitter (#6982). Registry-liveness remains paused until #6537's feeder ships and a beat is measured. All three new/newly-fed web beats (web_zot_consumer, web_nic_guard, git_data_prd) are arm-gated by the automated measure-then-arm PATCH in apply-web-platform-infra.yml (ADR-117 amendment #6438). ALSO a per-host origin absence detector that probes each web host's CF-proxied hostname (web-N.app.soleur.ai/health) directly, so a dead/never-booted host pages with per-host attribution the round-robin monitors cannot give (#5933 Item 1). Validation is HTTP-01 against GitHub's origin, which is why remediation must transiently flip apex+www to DNS-only — a Cloudflare-proxied record makes LE see CF anycast instead of GitHub's 185.199.x. description.txt: Zero-trust inbound access — no exposed ports. ONE tunnel (tunnel.tf) with THREE ingress rules (deploy./ssh./registry.). DETERMINISM IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not one-connector: since #6594/PR-A all three ingress services are ORIGIN-RELATIVE (deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000, ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22, registry. → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000), so whichever connector replica CF selects proxies to the correct origin (ADR-114 I2 discharged for all three). This — not 'localhost: means this host' — is what makes the management plane deterministic. NOT AN INVARIANT: the earlier 'exactly ONE connector, ADR-114 I1 enforced #6425' claim is FALSE in production. The server.tf web_tunnel_connector gate lives at cloud-init create-time user_data only, and hcloud_server.web carries ignore_changes=[user_data], so it never re-runs on a booted host. (Historical: web-2 booted 2026-07-13 BEFORE the gate merged 2026-07-15, so TWO connectors were live and measured; web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463) and var.web_hosts is now single-host.) I1 is a construction-time gate presented as a runtime precondition — it governs only future fresh hosts, and that stays true after #6441: the NIC gate added there is FIRST-BOOT (runcmd is once-per-instance), so a fresh connector host now waits for its private address before registering and DEFERS rather than aborting on timeout, but no gate re-runs on a host that is already up. CF binds ingress to a TUNNEL and picks a connector per edge colo; before the origin-relative pin a SECOND connector silently made every non-fan-out route (deploy-status, inngest-liveness, infra-config WRITEs, ssh.) answer from whichever replica the caller's colo selected — #6425 (16h of false inngest-down alarms), #6594 (a false-green infra-config apply), #6416. Origin-relative ingress makes that harmless: the coin flip no longer determines correctness. Standing guard: the */15 connector census in scheduled-inngest-health.yml (vantage-independent; a response-poll is colo-sticky and proves nothing). Management plane only: app.soleur.ai does NOT traverse the tunnel (direct CF-proxied A record, dns.tf); no cloudflared on zot/git-data/inngest (ADR-096).

description.txt: Shared bare git repos (objects/refs) over the private net; per-user worktrees stay host-local on NVMe. The git-data host holds the per-ref monotonic max generation and writer-side-CAS-rejects stale lease writes (ADR-068). NOT YET PROVISIONED (#6977): this element is DECLARED in IaC and the host has never existed — an authenticated `terraform state list` returns zero git-data members — so every behaviour described here is the TARGET state, not the live one. It remains unborn until the gated `git-data-host-create` dispatch runs. The birth-readiness interlock that held that route is RELEASED by #6982, which ships the off-host emitter (ADR-149 item 1): the host now emits boot-stage fatals to Sentry from a baked DSN, a `stage:boot_complete` signal the birth job POLLS, and gc faults to Better Stack — so a green apply and a dark host are no longer indistinguishable. What holds the route now is MECHANICAL, not prose: `git_data_rung2_rehearsal_gate` (#6982 A3) runs in the same dispatch job before any provider is contacted and refuses unless `git-data-rung2-boot-evidence.env` attests a rung-2 boot rehearsal hash-bound to the CURRENT template — a hash-of-hashes over the cloud-init plus every `file()`-bound payload, so the evidence self-invalidates on any later edit to what ships. That file is absent, so a dispatch exits 1. #7025 shipped the gated rehearsal ROUTE that produces it (a separate Terraform root + `workflow_dispatch`), deliberately UNFIRED — a PR merges atomically, so evidence committed alongside its own harness would attest a rehearsal that never ran. The runbook banner is the THIRD hold, not the only one. AT REST: the target store is PLAINTEXT ext4 (`hcloud_volume.git_data`, `format = "ext4"`, no LUKS apparatus) — a fresh `hcloud_volume.git_data_luks` cutover target is declared alongside it (git-data-luks.tf) but is not the live store (`GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` gates the cutover). The 60 GB store volume re-fills ONLY from a fresh CI dual-push — NOT from GHCR. Its previous description as a 'disposable GHCR mirror' with an 'atomic GHCR fallback' is RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (#7071): the sibling ghcr node in this same enumeration is now marked DEAD AS A FALLBACK (read PAT revoked -> 401, minter disabled -> 403 DENIED), so an emptied store leaves NO registry any host can pull from until CI re-pushes. The blobs stay reproducible, so this is a recoverability property, never a free one — every recut/replace of this volume takes production's only pull path offline for the gap. Hosts pull the SAME @sha256 digests here (crane-copy from CI preserves them); cosign verifies the zot-stored .sig offline against the unchanged pinned root. Plain-HTTP on the private net (integrity via cosign digest-pinning, not TLS). AT REST: guest-side LUKS, CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING (`hcloud_volume.registry` is declared RAW — no `format` — and cloud-init-registry.yml luksFormats/luksOpens it as /dev/mapper/registry, keyed by random_password.registry_luks via doppler_secret.registry_luks_key). The LIVE device is still plaintext ext4 until the guarded `registry-luks-recut` workflow_dispatch is fired; that vehicle shipped UNFIRED (#6929), so this is a code-declared posture, NOT a live-verified one. Low sensitivity (our own OCI blobs + cosign signatures, no user/repo data); integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not at-rest encryption (encryption-posture-ledger.json)

This is STRUCTURAL, not a lapsed chore: App installation tokens authenticate docker login but are DENIED docker pull on private repo-linked packages (ADR-088 arm-b), so no zero-touch GHCR pull credential can exist — only a personal one. Consequence: zot is the SOLE pull path and the CI zot mirror is now release-blocking (ADR-096 amendment 2026-07-30). Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.

description.txt: Zero-trust inbound access — no exposed ports. ONE tunnel (tunnel.tf) with THREE ingress rules (deploy./ssh./registry.). DETERMINISM IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not one-connector: since #6594/PR-A all three ingress services are ORIGIN-RELATIVE (deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000, ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22, registry. → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000), so whichever connector replica CF selects proxies to the correct origin (ADR-114 I2 discharged for all three). This — not 'localhost: means this host' — is what makes the management plane deterministic. NOT AN INVARIANT: the earlier 'exactly ONE connector, ADR-114 I1 enforced #6425' claim is FALSE in production. The server.tf web_tunnel_connector gate lives at cloud-init create-time user_data only, and hcloud_server.web carries ignore_changes=[user_data], so it never re-runs on a booted host. (Historical: web-2 booted 2026-07-13 BEFORE the gate merged 2026-07-15, so TWO connectors were live and measured; web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463) and var.web_hosts is now single-host.) I1 is a construction-time gate presented as a runtime precondition — it governs only future fresh hosts, and that stays true after #6441: the NIC gate added there is FIRST-BOOT (runcmd is once-per-instance), so a fresh connector host now waits for its private address before registering and DEFERS rather than aborting on timeout, but no gate re-runs on a host that is already up. CF binds ingress to a TUNNEL and picks a connector per edge colo; before the origin-relative pin a SECOND connector silently made every non-fan-out route (deploy-status, inngest-liveness, infra-config WRITEs, ssh.) answer from whichever replica the caller's colo selected — #6425 (16h of false inngest-down alarms), #6594 (a false-green infra-config apply), #6416. Origin-relative ingress makes that harmless: the coin flip no longer determines correctness. Standing guard: the */15 connector census in scheduled-inngest-health.yml (vantage-independent; a response-poll is colo-sticky and proves nothing). Management plane only: app.soleur.ai does NOT traverse the tunnel (direct CF-proxied A record, dns.tf); no cloudflared on zot/git-data/inngest (ADR-096).

What holds the route now is MECHANICAL, not prose: `git_data_rung2_rehearsal_gate` (#6982 A3) runs in the same dispatch job before any provider is contacted and refuses unless `git-data-rung2-boot-evidence.env` attests a rung-2 boot rehearsal hash-bound to the CURRENT template — a hash-of-hashes over the cloud-init plus every `file()`-bound payload, so the evidence self-invalidates on any later edit to what ships. That file is absent, so a dispatch exits 1. #7025 shipped the gated rehearsal ROUTE that produces it (a separate Terraform root + `workflow_dispatch`), deliberately UNFIRED — a PR merges atomically, so evidence committed alongside its own harness would attest a rehearsal that never ran. The runbook banner is the THIRD hold, not the only one. description.txt: External uptime/heartbeat monitoring (BetterStackHQ/better-uptime) AND a Logs warehouse (source 2457081, ClickHouse-SQL-queryable) that CI polls read-only. Apex + inngest + registry-disk heartbeats, plus (#6438/#6548) TWO new per-host web heartbeats — web_zot_consumer (the zot-consumer serviceability probe, #6438 §1) and web_nic_guard (the §3 private-NIC-guard liveness beat, #6438 §3), both for_each var.web_hosts — and git-data, whose git_data_prd beat is FED by the web-host consumer probe (#6548) but is **deliberately NOT armed** — #6982 (D-HB) withdrew the plan to arm it, and #6548 alone now owns the decision. Three reasons, any one disqualifying: the `arm_one` call for it lives in the PER-MERGE apply job, so creating the heartbeat would make an unborn flag-off host's health a merge-blocking dependency for the whole repository; a TCP connect-and-close to :22 proves the port is OPEN, not that git transport SERVES, and sshd is up before runcmd runs — so a host whose LUKS never mounted answers on :22 and beats GREEN, installing a green light over the exact failure the interlock exists to catch; and the object pool may be at 10/10. git-data's boot correctness is instead reported HOST-SIDE by its own emitter (#6982). Registry-liveness remains paused until #6537's feeder ships and a beat is measured. All three new/newly-fed web beats (web_zot_consumer, web_nic_guard, git_data_prd) are arm-gated by the automated measure-then-arm PATCH in apply-web-platform-infra.yml (ADR-117 amendment #6438). ALSO a per-host origin absence detector that probes each web host's CF-proxied hostname (web-N.app.soleur.ai/health) directly, so a dead/never-booted host pages with per-host attribution the round-robin monitors cannot give (#5933 Item 1). The Logs source receives SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK + SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC self-reports from the deny-all registry host AND SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC from web-1 (the §3 web-host guard, detect+emit+alarm, NO reboot — ADR-123) and is polled from GitHub Actions via betterstack-query.sh for the zot restart-loop recurrence alarm (#6291) + follow-through soak probes — log-content recurrence alarms are in-repo GH-cron pollers, not native Better Stack alerts (ADR-096).

Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.
